signals.text: The wordcount command reports the number of words and visible characters in the input file, but not how many lines it has; users want the line count too.
Every successful run of `wordcount PATH` should print the line count on the same stdout line, in the form `words: <N> characters: <M> lines: <L>`.
signals.possible_indication: The existing `words: <N> characters: <M>` output contract changes, so anything documenting or checking the old line (README, tests) is affected.

signals.text: The line count is always printed: no new flag or option, and the single positional PATH invocation stays as it is.
signals.possible_indication: The scope is limited to output content, not the CLI's argument interface.

signals.text: A line is a terminated segment: every boundary that Python's str.splitlines() recognises counts as a line terminator (including lone CR, U+2028 and form feed), CRLF counts as one terminator, and an unterminated final segment is not counted.
signals.possible_indication: This is deliberately broader than literal `wc -l`, which counts only LF characters; users who compare output with `wc -l` will see different numbers on files with other separators.

signals.text: A file containing 'a', LF, 'b' reports 1 line, because the final 'b' has no terminator.
A whitespace-only file such as LF LF reports 2 lines, even though it reports 0 words and 0 characters.
signals.possible_indication: The line count is independent of the word and character rules; whitespace-only input is not treated as empty for line counting.

signals.text: A file containing 'a', CR, LF reports 1 line: CRLF is a single line break, not two.

DISCOVER.core_issue: Users of the wordcount CLI can see the word and visible-character counts of a file but cannot see how many lines it contains, so they have to use a separate tool to get it.
DISCOVER.impact_value: Users get a complete count of a file (words, characters, lines) from one invocation. The line count uses a clearly defined, Unicode-aware boundary rule instead of leaving it to whatever tool they would otherwise use.
DISCOVER.discovery_method: Written feature intent from the project owner, refined through one clarification round. In that round the human fixed the line-boundary rule, the whitespace-only behaviour, the output format and the invocation.
DISCOVER.pattern_dependencies: The missing line count is the core opportunity. The line-boundary definition determines what number appears in the new `lines: <L>` field, so the output-format change depends on that rule being settled. The rule is independent of the existing word and character rules, which stay unchanged.

pattern_narratives.applies_to: The `wordcount PATH` command's successful stdout output line
pattern_narratives.frequency: Every successful invocation of the command
pattern_narratives.severity: Moderate: a feature gap, not a defect. Existing output keeps working, but its format will change.
pattern_narratives.confidence: High: the output format and always-on behaviour were confirmed explicitly by the human.
pattern_narratives.current_state: The command prints exactly `words: <N> characters: <M>` and gives no line information. Users must count lines with another tool.

pattern_narratives.applies_to: How lines are counted in any decoded UTF-8 input file, including empty, whitespace-only, CRLF and Unicode-separator files
pattern_narratives.frequency: Applies to every file. The edge cases (unterminated final segment, CRLF, U+2028, form feed, lone CR) show up whenever files come from mixed platforms or contain Unicode text.
pattern_narratives.severity: High for correctness: an ambiguous rule would produce counts that users and tests disagree on.
pattern_narratives.confidence: High: the human answered each boundary question and explicitly confirmed that the rule is broader than `wc -l`.
pattern_narratives.current_state: No line-counting rule exists in the project yet. The rule is now defined only in the clarified requirements.

DISCOVER.Should the line count follow `wc -l` (co: Follow the terminated-line convention: a followed by LF followed by b reports 1; do not count an unterminated final segment. Use the broader separators specified below.
DISCOVER.What should a whitespace-only file such: 2 lines. The human explicitly confirmed this correction.
DISCOVER.Which line terminators count as line bre: Every boundary Python str.splitlines() recognizes, with CRLF counted once. The human confirmed combining broader separators with not counting an unterminated final line.
DISCOVER.Should the line count always be printed: Always print the line count, with no new flag, retaining the single-PATH invocation.
